definitions.explanation: Having a rough or unrefined texture with large particles or loose weave.
Lacking precision or refinement in work or behavior.

examples.english: This cloth has a coarse weave.

examples.japanese: {粗|あら}い⟦{塩|しお}→塩：00887_shio⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{使|つか}って→使う：00473_tsukau⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
⟦{仕事|しごと}→仕事：00480_shigoto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{粗|あら}いので、⟦やり{直|なお}して→やり直す：03172_yarinaosu⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Your work is sloppy, so please redo it.

examples.japanese: {粗|あら}い{砂|すな}が{靴|くつ}の{中|なか}に{入|はい}った。
examples.english: Coarse sand got into my shoes.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{性格|せいかく}は{良|よ}いが、{仕事|しごと}が{粗|あら}い。
examples.english: He has a good personality, but his work is sloppy.

examples.japanese: {粗|あら}い{計算|けいさん}でもだいたいの{数字|すうじ}はわかる。
examples.english: Even with a rough calculation, you can get an approximate figure.

notes:
{粗|あら}い is an i-adjective describing coarseness of texture or crudeness of quality.

FORMS:
- Adverbial: {粗|あら}く
- Noun form: {粗|あら}さ (coarseness)

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {目|め}が{粗|あら}い (coarse weave/mesh)
- {粗|あら}い{塩|しお} (coarse salt)
- {仕事|しごと}が{粗|あら}い (sloppy work)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {粗|あら}い vs. {荒|あら}い: Both read あらい, but {粗|あら}い refers to texture/quality (coarse, crude), while {荒|あら}い refers to intensity/behavior (rough, wild, violent).

ORTHOGRAPHY:
The distinction between {粗|あら} and {荒|あら} is important but often confused in casual writing.
